newsitem.title: UGANDA: Uganda coffee sales jump in December, prices down.
newsitem.headline: Uganda coffee sales jump in December, prices down.

text.p: Ugandan coffee sales jumped sharply in December 1996 from the previous month but prices fell, the state coffee authority said.

In a monthly report, the Uganda Coffee Development Authority (UCDA) said heavy selling was attributed to "stiff competition associated with free market systems, removal of coffee stabilisation tax and high levels of opening stocks."
UCDA gave a provisional total of 985,403 60-kg bags of coffee contracted for sale in December versus only 353,960 in November.
The November UCDA figure was well below a provisional estimate of 436,261 bags it gave earlier but still slightly up on 340,000 bags sold in October.
Robusta Screen 15 (standard) grade dominated the market, contributing 63.7 percent of the total. Around 88 percent of Ugandan coffee exports are robusta with 12 percent arabicas.

Local prices ranged between 700 and 900 shillings per kg FAQ (fair average quality) while (lower grade) kiboko prices ranged from 350 to 450 shillings. Arabica parchment prices ranged from 1,000 to 1,100 shillings per kg.

Prices were lower following falls on international markets, the UCDA said. On average, November dry cherries prices ranged between 400 and 500 shillings per kg while those of FAQ and parchment ranged between 900-1,050 shillings and 1,120-1,250 shillings respectively, according to UCDA figures.
UCDA said it was expected that prices would continue on a downward spiral in January as more of the crop comes on the international markets, especially from Asia and Latin America.

However, the lower price trend could be salvaged by a meeting of coffee producers called by Brazil on January 23 which is expected to yield positive results on an agreement to cut exports in the first half of 1997, according to the UCDA.

"The meeting is expected to dwell mostly on analysis of market information and assess the implementation of the export programme in the first six months," UCDA said. --Nairobi Newsroom ++254-2 330-261.
